elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The Company, as Customer, may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The Company must provide ninety (90) days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is required.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The existing language permits either Party, including HDI, to terminate on ninety days' written notice and does not expressly restrict HDI's termination date to the end of a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Company may terminate for convenience on ninety (90) days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is expressly capped at three months of the fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: HDI may terminate under the either-Party provision on ninety days' notice, without an operative restriction requiring termination to occur only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The either-Party termination provision requires ninety (90) days' written notice from HDI.
